body:
_Migrated from issue #1354, filed 2026-08-04._

Found by the v4.1.29 pre-tag refuter gate.

#1325 fixed right-to-left page turning in the **epub** reader, and that fix verified clean on
every cell driven (desktop + mobile, real and synthetic books, keyboard, screen-reader names,
LTR control). But `frontend/src/pages/NativeReader.tsx` `ComicViewer` (~lines 110-120) is
untouched and still hard-wires:

- left zone → `Previous page` / `go(-1)`, right zone → `Next page` / `go(1)`
- `ArrowRight` → +1, `ArrowLeft` → −1

Japanese manga is *the* archetypal right-to-left reading experience, and it's delivered as
CBZ/CBR through this component, not through the epub reader. So for manga readers the page
turn is still backwards.

## Why this isn't a one-line copy of the epub fix

CBZ/CBR has no `page-progression-direction` equivalent. The nearest signal is ComicInfo.xml's
`<Manga>` element (`YesAndRightToLeft` is the meaningful value), which not every archive
carries. So this needs a detection decision — ComicInfo.xml when present, and some fallback
(per-book setting? language? user preference?) when it isn't — rather than reusing the epub
path's `packaging.metadata.direction`.

Also worth picking up in the same change: that component's chevrons lack `aria-hidden`, unlike
the epub reader's, so a screen reader announces the decorative glyph alongside the button name.

The v4.1.29 note has been narrowed to say the fix is in the ebook reader, so it no longer
implies comics are covered.
title: Comics/manga reader still pages left-to-right for right-to-left titles
